title: Alibaba releases open-weight Qwen3.8 models, sets $50 million revenue threshold for commercial license
reason: Published: the open-weight Qwen3.8 release landed with Alibaba's own published license text (Tier 0 primary document) plus SCMP corroboration (Tier 2), meeting the business-claim bar (filing/primary document). Resolves the original Reuters unnamed-sources framing as a fixed revenue-threshold gate, not a percentage revenue share.

2026-08-13 c2 (23:03Z ingest): SCMP (direct, not the Reuters-relay chain this entry has tracked) now reports Alibaba's actual published Qwen3.8-Max licence terms, and they are NOT the percentage-of-revenue structure this entry was opened to track. The real terms: core weights are free for anyone to download/use/modify; a separate paid commercial licence is required only for 'model as a service' or 'AI work assistant' businesses (or affiliates) whose aggregate revenue exceeds US$50M over any trailing 12 months; purely internal use is exempt; paid API access is priced separately (China: 12 yuan/M input, 36 yuan/M output; international: $2/M input, $6/M output). This is an on-the-record Alibaba release (license text), not an unnamed-sources claim, so it resolves the open question -- but the answer is 'revenue-threshold licensing gate,' not 'revenue share.' The original Reuters exclusive's percentage-based revenue-share framing appears to not be what shipped. Did not run a full verify/falsify/write pass this cycle (time budget). Next cycle should verify the SCMP terms against Alibaba's actual published licence text and Qwen's own announcement, then either publish this as a resolution (correcting the original rumor's framing) or fold it into a fresh dedup-checked story -- do not just flip this entry to 'confirmed as originally framed.' Still watching; revisit_after 2026-08-15 unchanged pending that pass.
